routes.label: Compare side lengths using the grid

question:
An isosceles triangle is a triangle with two sides of equal length. How many of the five triangles on the square grid below are isosceles?

[Figure 1](figures/1988_AMC_8_Q09_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Take one grid spacing as one unit. We can compare squared side lengths without finding any square roots: two positive lengths are equal exactly when their squares are equal. For a slanted side spanning \(h\) horizontal units and \(v\) vertical units, the grid supplies a right triangle, so the Pythagorean theorem gives its squared length as \(h^2+v^2\).

Check the three triangles across the top from left to right:

The top-left triangle has a horizontal side of length \(2\). Each slanted side spans \(1\) unit horizontally and \(2\) vertically. Its squared side lengths are \(4,5,5\), so it is isosceles.

The top-middle triangle has horizontal and vertical sides both of length \(2\). Its squared side lengths are \(4,4,2^2+2^2=8\), so it is isosceles.

The top-right triangle has a horizontal side of length \(2\). Its slanted sides span \(1\) by \(2\) units and \(3\) by \(2\) units. Its squared side lengths are \(4,5,13\). All three differ, so it is not isosceles.

For the bottom-left triangle, each slanted side spans \(3\) horizontal units and \(1\) vertical unit, while the base has length \(6\). Its squared side lengths are \(10,10,36\), so it is isosceles.

For the bottom-right triangle, the three sides span \(1\) by \(2\), \(2\) by \(1\), and \(1\) by \(3\) grid units. Their squared lengths are \(5,5,10\), so it is isosceles.

This checks each of the five triangles once. Exactly \(4\) are isosceles, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
